answer: Pay rewards on a square-root curve: an identity's payout grows with the square root of its verified work, not linearly, so splitting one agent's effort across a thousand fake identities earns far less in total than doing it as one. Like a comet that shines only as a single body, or an opal valued whole rather than shattered, the math punishes fragmentation. The fable that more identities mean more rewards is false by design: a Sybil operator pays the full setup cost of a thousand identities and still collects less than one honest agent.
